title: Control plane slate-shift digest: routing / auth / quotas sync
body:
Overview:
This is a mid-sprint sync focused on three cross-cutting areas: routing resiliency, auth token throttling, and quota fallthrough behavior. The meeting was intentionally short (30m) to align action items before tomorrow's canary. Notes capture data from last 72h and proposed mitigations.

Attendees:
- Aisha B. (owner)
- Liam O
- Mateo R
- Sun-hee P
- Ravi P (SRE)
- Guest: Elena (Solutions Eng)

Metrics snapshot (last 72h):
- Controlplane p95 decision latency: 73ms -> spiked to 210ms during 2027-09-14 03:00 UTC under heavy quota-eval.
- Routing fallbacks triggered: 1.8% of requests (target <0.5%).
- Auth token re-issuance rate: 4.1% of sessions (baseline 0.9%) correlated with KMS transient errors.
- Quotas: 12 customers bumped into soft-throttle window; 3 hit hard-fallthrough.

Highlights / Findings:
1) Batching experiment (adaptive batching v2) reduced average CPU by ~9% on exec-nodes but increased queuing for short-lived requests; improves cost but worsens p95 for <150ms SLO tiers.
2) One large customer (acct-6821) had a malformed quota header leading to repeated fallback attempts — queue thrash amplified by routing affinity.
3) KMS region failover logic did not surface fast enough: auth backoff jitter was too conservative, causing burst of token re-issuance attempts.
4) Quota policy matcher had a hot codepath: regex-based tenant id extraction performed ~2.7M ops/min in worst window.

Blockers:
- Need a quick patch to reduce regex cost in quota matcher (blocking PLT-3510).
- Can't reproduce KMS transient failure locally; need logs from customer region and SRE to run a replay.
- Canary gating for adaptive batching requires a dedicated LB rule which infra team must provision (PR #4123 pending approval).

Decisions made:
- Roll forward with adaptive batching v2 for internal-only traffic on canary circle A (10% of capacity) but keep fallback to pre-batch path on latency breach >120ms for two consecutive 30s windows.
- Short-term: add conservative token backoff (exponential with capped jitter) and increase KMS retry multiplier for region fallback path.
- Quota matcher: ship a defensive fallback that treats unparseable tenant headers as "defer-to-default-policy" and emit a metric to isolate offending customers.

Action items (owner / due):
- Aisha: Draft rollout playbook for adaptive batching canary (include abort criteria and rollback steps) — due 2027-09-18.
- Mateo: Implement regex optimization + unit tests for quota matcher; open canary flag. (JIRA PLT-3510) — due 2027-09-20.
- Sun-hee: Add KMS retry multiplier change and run regression in staging; coordinate with SRE for log collection — due 2027-09-18.
- Liam: Push infra PR to add canary LB rule and document IP ranges for circle A; chase approvals on PR 4123 — due 2027-09-16 (in flight).
- Ravi (SRE): Provide trace dump for 2027-09-14 spike and enable detailed auth traces for region eu-west-1 for 48h — due 2027-09-17.

Follow-ups / Notes:
- Mateo flagged potential performance regression from a previous refactor (refactor-ctl-2027-06). He will include a microbenchmark as part of PLT-3510.
- Elena to ask CS to anonymize customer request patterns from acct-6821 so we can safely replay load in staging.
- We will run a synthetic traffic sweep tomorrow 06:00-07:30 UTC targeting small-Latency SLO buckets to validate the latency gating logic.

Runbook snippet (for on-call):
- If routing fallbacks exceed 0.8% for 10m:
  1) Toggle fallback route weight away from affinity path to generic-path-2 (console -> Operations -> Routing -> Weights).
  2) If p95 > 150ms after weight switch, abort adaptive batching for canary and notify infra on-call.
  3) If auth re-issuance rate >2% escalate to SRE with trace id sample.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we need permanent quota-match caching keyed by tenant-id to avoid regex cost? Cache invalidation strategy TBD.
- How much does the adaptive batching profile degrade tail latency for multi-tenant noisy neighbors? Need a steady-state 24h test.
- Risk: canary LB rule rollout timeline is dependent on infra approvals; if delayed, we'll rerun on non-production pool which has a smaller signal.

Next sync: 2027-09-20 10:00 UTC (short check-in) — agenda: canary readiness review, PLT-3510 status, SRE trace findings.

Attachments / links referenced in discussion: JIRA PLT-3482 (routing fallback investigation), JIRA PLT-3510 (quota matcher perf), PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4123, Slack thread: #platform-routing (see thread pinned 2027-09-15), Confluence sketch: controlplane-quota-cache-proposal.

Quick wins for today:
- Mateo to toggle a low-risk regex fallback that changes garbage tenant headers to default_policy and emit metric to isolate offenders (5-10m deploy window).
- Sun-hee to bump KMS retry multiplier in staging and confirm auth traces appear (20m task).

End of digest.
